name: io.github.logan1085/evallab
title: Eval Lab
description: Your agent drafts eval cases; you grade them; it gets your verdicts and fixes its rubric.

tools.name: request_human_review
tools.description: Use this when building or revising an eval set, LLM-as-judge prompt or rubric, and you need the user's own judgment on example outputs. Send the rubric and 1 to 50 cases (input, output, optional context, optional verdict and reason from your own judge). Returns a review link for the user, a review id and a read token. Show the link to the user and ask them to grade, then call wait_for_human_review with the id and token. Your judge verdicts are hidden from the user until they grade each case, so their call is not anchored on yours. For a follow-up round after revising the rubric, pass parent_id with the previous review id.

title.description: Short name for this batch, e.g. "Refund agent evals, round 1".

product.description: One line on the system under test, e.g. "Support bot for a bike shop".

rubric.description: The current rubric, one rule per entry. May be empty if you want the user to grade from instinct first.

input.description: What the user said, or the task given to the system under test.

context.description: Optional: retrieved docs, tool results, or the expected answer.

judge_verdict.description: Optional: your LLM judge's verdict on this case.

cases.description: 1 to 50 cases. Pick the ones you are least sure about.

parent_id.description: The previous review id, when this is a revised round.

tools.name: get_human_judgments
tools.description: Read the user's pass / fixable / fail verdicts and reasons for a review created with request_human_review, without waiting. Returns progress, every verdict so far, the cases where the user disagreed with your judge, the agreement rate, and a next step. Treat the user's verdicts as ground truth for the eval set; disagreements show where the rubric or judge prompt needs a new rule.

tools.name: wait_for_human_review
tools.description: Call right after showing the user the review link. Waits until the user has finished grading (or timeout_seconds passes, at most 240), then returns the same result as get_human_judgments. If it returns before the user is done, call it again or ask the user how it is going.

timeout_seconds.description: How long to wait, in seconds. Default 120, at most 240.
